exact_current_steps.1.1:
Extend the real-linear supplier $R$ to complex mean-zero tests by $R_{\mathbb C}(h_1+ih_2)=Rh_1+iRh_2$, where $h_1,h_2$ are real. Their integrals both vanish. Real linearity makes this extension complex-linear; applying the supplier bounds to the two parts preserves fixed-support continuity, the same output-support set, and $\operatorname{div}R_{\mathbb C}h=h$. In the rest of the proof $R$ denotes this extension. On $U=(0,\infty)\times\Omega$, $u\in L^2_{\rm loc}$ and $u\otimes u\in L^1_{\rm loc}$. For a compact $K\subset U$, let $p_{m,K}$ be the maximum of the suprema on $K$ of all component derivatives of order at most $m$. The same local estimate $|\int_K f\psi|\le\|f\|_{L^1(K)}p_{0,K}(\psi)$ shows that the regular pairings of $u$ and $u\otimes u$ are continuous on every fixed-support test space, hence are distributions. The residual functional
$$\langle T,\psi\rangle=\int_U\bigl(u\cdot\partial_t\psi+(u\otimes u):\nabla_x\psi+\nu u\cdot\Delta_x\psi\bigr)\,dt\,dx$$
is well-defined and satisfies
$$|\langle T,\psi\rangle|\le C_d\bigl(\|u\|_{L^1(K)}+\|u\otimes u\|_{L^1(K)}\bigr)p_{1,K}(\psi)+C_d\nu\|u\|_{L^1(K)}p_{2,K}(\psi)$$
for every test supported in $K$. Thus its absolute value is a seminorm whose restriction to each fixed-support test space is continuous; by the test-function topology in [F4], $T$ is a spacetime distribution. By [F3], this formula is exactly the residual $-\partial_tu-\operatorname{div}(u\otimes u)+\nu\Delta u$ of those regular distributions. For a scalar test $\phi(t,x)$ put $\phi_0=\phi-\theta(x)\int_\Omega\phi(t,y)dy$ and define
$$\langle\pi,\phi\rangle=-\langle T,R_x\phi_0\rangle.$$
The map $R$ is applied at each time. The spatial supports of $\phi_0(t,\cdot)$ lie in one compact subset of $\Omega$, since they are contained in the union of the spatial support of $\phi$ and $\operatorname{supp}\theta$. For each time derivative order, $t\mapsto\partial_t^j\phi_0(t,\cdot)$ is continuous in every fixed-support test seminorm. Linearity and continuity of $R$ on that fixed-support space imply that $t\mapsto R\phi_0(t,\cdot)$ is smooth with derivatives $R\partial_t^j\phi_0$; the support condition in [F2] puts all outputs in one compact spatial set. Thus $R_x\phi_0$ is a smooth spacetime test with compact temporal support, and the displayed functional is continuous by the same fixed-support estimate for $T$. It is a distribution. [given, F1, F2, F3, F4]
exact_current_steps.2.1:
For a compact smooth vector test $\psi$, $h=\operatorname{div}_x\psi$ has spatial integral zero by coordinate integration, so $h\in D_0(\Omega)$ and $\psi-Rh$ is compactly supported, smooth, and divergence free. By [F1], $\langle T,\psi-Rh\rangle=0$. Moreover,
$$\langle\nabla_x\pi,\psi\rangle=-\langle\pi,h\rangle=\langle T,Rh\rangle=\langle T,\psi\rangle.$$
Substituting the definition of $T$ proves the full distributional momentum equation. The normalization holds because $(a\theta)_0=0$. [given, F1, F2, F3, step 1.1]
exact_current_steps.3.1: If $\pi_1,\pi_2$ have the same spatial gradient, their difference $q$ has $\nabla_xq=0$. For an arbitrary scalar spacetime test $\phi$, put $a(t)=\int_\Omega\phi(t,x)dx$ and $\phi_0=\phi-a\theta$. Step 1.1 gives a spacetime vector test $R_x\phi_0$ with spatial divergence $\phi_0$. Hence $\langle q,\phi_0\rangle=-\langle\nabla_xq,R_x\phi_0\rangle=0$, and $\langle q,\phi\rangle=\langle q,a\theta\rangle=0$ by the shared normalization. Thus $q=0$, proving uniqueness conditional on [F2]. [given, F2, step 1.1, step 2.1] ∎

complexification_check.support: Real and imaginary parts have the same input support bound K; the single supplier output-support bound Kprime serves both parts, so their sum remains supported in Kprime.
complexification_check.continuity: Every output seminorm is bounded by the sum of the two real-output seminorms. Each real-part input seminorm is bounded by the complex input seminorm. The finite sum of fixed-support continuity estimates proves complex fixed-support continuity.

complexification_check.solenoidal_annihilation: For a complex solenoidal test, real and imaginary parts are real solenoidal tests. The real velocity residual annihilates each by the weak identity, so complex linearity extends annihilation. This is an immediate consequence of current residual definition, not a new supplier hypothesis.
